cards.text: Meanwhile, out on the battlefield, there's still a war on. David stayed back in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 11:1), but Joab, the commander of his army (2 Samuel 8:16), is fighting against Rabbah of the Ammonites.

cards.question: Joab is fighting against Rabbah of the Ammonites. What does he capture?

cards.text: No group chat on the battlefield, friend. So Joab sends messengers back to David with an update from the front.

cards.question: In his message, Joab tells David he has captured the city's water supply.

cards.text: Then Joab tells David what to do next: gather the rest of the troops, lay siege to the city and capture it. And then Joab adds a little P.S. that I would NEVER put in a note to my boss.

cards.question: Joab tells David to come and capture Rabbah. What does Joab say will happen otherwise?

answers.text: Joab will capture it and it will be named after him
The Ammonites will win back the royal fortress
The troops will give up and head back home

cards.text: WHOA, Joab! That's like a coworker texting you, "Come finish this project, or my name's going on it." So David gets moving.

cards.question: David assembles ___ of the troops and goes to Rabbah.

cards.text: David goes to Rabbah, fights against it and CAPTURES it! Funny how fast things get done when somebody threatens to put their name on your work.

cards.question: Rabbah has fallen. What does David take from the head of the Ammonites' king?
The king's crown weighed a talent of ___ and was set with precious stones.

cards.text: Then that crown is placed on David's head. A TALENT of gold up there, friend, and I can barely keep this chef's hat on straight!

cards.question: Besides the crown, David takes a great amount of plunder from Rabbah.

cards.text: The fighting's over, but David isn't finished at Rabbah yet. He brings out the people who were there in the city.

cards.question: David brings out the people of Rabbah. What does he do with them?

answers.text: Puts them to work with tools and at brick kilns
Sends them away to live in a far land
Makes them stand guard over the city walls

cards.question: David puts the people of Rabbah to work, but he leaves the other Ammonite cities alone.
With the Ammonite cities handled, where do David and all his troops go?

findings.problem: "a little P.S. that I would NEVER put in a note to my boss" says Papa Dorin has a boss he writes notes to. His backstory gives him no boss. The only one over him is the Most High, so the line either adds something new to his world or drifts toward calling God his boss. A general version keeps the joke, like "a P.S. nobody should ever put in a note to the boss."

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: "Funny how fast things get done when somebody threatens to put their name on your work" says David acted because of Joab's threat. Verse 29 only says "So David assembled all the troops." The text doesn't say David moved because of the naming line or that Joab meant it as a threat. This line also repeats card 7's joke, so cutting the motive loses nothing.

rule.text: Reasons. He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.
